name: Waldorf Microwave
description: Waldorf Microwave (1989) wavetable synthesizer, system software 2.00: every sound parameter of its System Exclusive Documentation, sent as a real-time sound edit, with Pull of the sound playing.

sources.title: Waldorf Microwave System Exclusive Documentation, system software version 2.00 revision 00 (1 March 1994)
sources.notes: The sound dump's byte table and its lists read by tools/profiles/waldorf/read-waldorf-text.mjs from MicrowaveSysex 2_0.txt (sha256 9f23a0cfcbf06c95ba80a1774595a4ee012e105570281d780f20937117bc96e0), https://downloads.waldorfmusic.com/cloud/index.php/s/weTqE3SkZzocxYe/download (Documentation EN/MicrowaveSysex 2_0.txt in the zip). Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/waldorf/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/waldorf/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is a byte of the document's sound dump, with its printed name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Parameter change: F0 3E 00 <dev> 60 <instrument> <parameter, two nibbles> <value> <CHK> F7, the parameter its byte in the sound dump (0 - 179), CHK the 7-bit sum of the bytes after 60. <dev> is the deviceId variable, the instrument's Device Number (0 unless set otherwise); its dumps are matched by it too.
No identity check: the document prints no identity reply.
The document is for system software 2.00. A Microwave on an earlier version has the same sound dump, but the parameters marked + have narrower ranges there and those marked * do nothing.

The Microwave answers the sound request with the sound playing, edits and all, which in Multi mode is the last instrument's selected: the document says to switch to Single (MIDI-Poly) mode before requesting. The edit goes to instrument 1's sound (instrument 0), which in Single mode is the sound playing.
The Microwave sends the same edit message (RTBP) when its Overflow Mode is Link and a sound parameter is changed on its panel; CEditor reads those by byte.

Read through this profile, the factory sound sets Waldorf publishes (mwsset1 - 4, 256 sounds from cartridge dumps) predate system software 2.00: bytes 144 and 169 - 174, unused before it, hold what was left there, so the LFO 2 phase shift and the wave and noise level modifiers read as values outside their lists in most of them. 60 of the 256 have characters below 20h in their names (0Ch, 19h - 1Fh), outside the 20h - 7Fh the document gives, read as ?.
Rows the document prints wrongly, given by the layout: 13 Osc 1 Modifier 2 Source, 14 Osc 1 Modifier 2 Amount.
Pull: Sound Dump Request (BPRR), the sound playing. 151 of 151 parameters are read back.

coverage.inboundControllers: parameter changes the instrument sends are read by byte; its control changes are not mapped
